content_of_post_to_comment:
I've spent years trying to become a disciplined person. Someone who works out, makes time for the things they want to do rather than just the things they feel like doing, and consistently works towards their goals.

I've achieved some pretty significant things over the past few years, and I tend to attribute them to hard work and a bit of luck. However, my biggest struggle — exercising regularly and getting in shape — is still very much an ongoing battle.

Recently, I started wondering whether I'm actually becoming more disciplined. And then I had another thought: maybe this is exactly what being disciplined feels like.

Maybe it's about constantly feeling like there's still so much work to do. Knowing that you fail more days than you'd like. Even knowing that something you've been pursuing for years hasn't shown any visible progress.

Perhaps the version of discipline I've imagined in my head — having everything under control, making constant progress, always staying on track — is just a fantasy.

I honestly don't know. So I'd like to ask those of you who consider yourselves disciplined people:

What does being disciplined actually feel like?
comment: I think discipline feels less like having everything under control and more like learning not to turn one bad day into a bad week. Also, progress in different areas doesn't happen at the same pace. You can be genuinely disciplined at work and still struggle with exercise because the habits, environment, and barriers are different. Maybe discipline isn't a personality trait you've either developed or haven't; it's something you keep rebuilding in specific areas.
